Digital Impression

Digital impressions are a modern alternative to traditional dental impressions. Instead of using trays filled with impression material, the dentist uses an intraoral scanner to capture a 3D image of the teeth and gums. From a patient’s perspective, digital impressions often provide a more comfortable and convenient experience.

1. Improved Comfort

Traditional impressions can be uncomfortable because the tray and material may cause:

* Gag reflex
* Bad taste
* Feeling of pressure
* Difficulty breathing temporarily

Digital impressions avoid bulky trays and putty-like materials, making the process easier and more pleasant for most patients.

2. Faster Procedure

Scanning usually takes only a few minutes. If an area is missed, the dentist can immediately rescan that part rather than repeating the whole impression. This saves chairside time and reduces patient inconvenience.

3. Better Accuracy

Patients benefit from improved accuracy because digital scans can reduce errors caused by:

* Material distortion
* Air bubbles
* Improper tray seating

More accurate impressions may lead to better-fitting crowns, bridges, aligners, dentures, and restorations.

4. Reduced Anxiety

Patients who fear dental procedures may feel less stressed because digital scanning is cleaner, less messy, and less invasive.

5. Convenience and Efficiency

Digital files can be sent instantly to dental laboratories, which may shorten treatment time and reduce the number of appointments.

🦷 Why are my teeth sensitive to hot or cold?

Do you feel a sharp pain when sipping hot coffee ☕ or enjoying ice cream 🍦? You might be dealing with tooth sensitivity.

👉 Common reasons include:
• Worn-out enamel (due to aggressive brushing or acidic foods)
• Gum recession exposing the root surface
• Tooth decay or cavities
• Cracked or chipped teeth
• Recent dental treatments (temporary sensitivity is normal)

👉 What’s actually happening?
The inner layer of your tooth (dentin) gets exposed, allowing heat or cold to reach the nerve — causing that sudden discomfort.

👉 How can you manage it?
✔ Use a desensitizing toothpaste
✔ Avoid very acidic or sugary foods
✔ Brush gently with a soft-bristle brush
✔ Don’t ignore persistent sensitivity

⚠️ Important: Sensitivity can sometimes be a sign of a deeper issue. Early diagnosis can save your tooth!

So, unfortunately, I had a really disappointing experience at DentHeal due to unprofessional behavior from one of the doctors. There was a prior issue regarding my father’s treatment, which he was unsatisfied with, and we were told that the amount would be adjusted towards my mother’s treatment. However, when we visited the clinic, the doctor who had originally treated my father was unavailable, and it was clear that things were not properly coordinated on their end.

While I was simply trying to explain the miscommunication and express my dissatisfaction, I was shocked by the extremely disrespectful attitude of Dr. Saba Siddiqui. Instead of listening calmly, she responded with hostility and spoke to me in a very rude tone. Since she was the one performing my mother’s treatment at the time, I had no trust in how she would proceed with the treatment after the way she spoke to me, so I had no choice but to stop the procedure midway and leave the clinic.

This kind of experience especially in a medical setting, where professionalism and respectful communication is a bare minimum, was extremely disappointing. I want to clearly state that I was polite throughout and only attempted to clarify the situation respectfully. At no point did I raise my voice or speak rudely. It’s disheartening to be treated that way simply for expressing valid concerns and trying to resolve a miscommunication.

Just because there are celebrities walking into the clinic doesn’t mean I should be spoken to with disrespect. If I’m coming in and paying that kind of money, I deserve to be treated with the same dignity and professionalism as anyone else.
